lockwood.name: Lockwood Memorial Library
about: Lockwood is UB's main research library.
It got its name from a 1929 gift of 500,000 dollars. Thomas and Marion Lockwood gave it in memory of their fathers.
The name moved campuses. The first Lockwood was a four-story Georgian building on South Campus, opened in 1935 and now called Abbott Hall.
In 1977 the name moved to the new North Campus library, which opened in June 1978.
It is about 237,000 square feet, was built for 9.37 million dollars, and was designed by the Chicago firm Harry Weese and Associates.
It began as a graduate library for the social sciences and humanities.
orientation: Lockwood has some hidden collections: the Polish Room, a Map Collection, an East Asian Collection, an International Leisure Reading Collection and a Juvenile Collection.
It is also a U.S. Government Documents depository.
Today it serves Arts and Sciences, Education, Engineering, Management and Social Work.
The Science and Engineering Information Center moved in during 2015.

nsc.name: Natural Sciences Complex
about: The Natural Sciences Complex, or NSC, opened in fall 1994 and cost 49.9 million dollars.
Its roof is often compared to a giant birthday cake. Each of the 128 labs in the research tower has its own exhaust system, so 128 exhaust cones stick up from the roof.
Its mix of dark and light brick and its big windows were a deliberate break from the older brown brick of North Campus, following the Student Union and the Center for the Arts.
It had a rough start. In July 1991, nine construction workers fell twelve feet when the supports under a concrete floor they were pouring collapsed.
It is about 307,000 square feet and was designed by Davis Brody and Associates.
orientation: NSC is two buildings in one.
One part is a two-story lecture building with five lecture halls that seat 150 to 350 people, plus five classrooms with 90 seats each.
Next to it is an eight-story research tower with 128 labs.
Look up at the roof to spot the 128 exhaust cones.

capen.name: Capen Hall
about: Capen Hall is UB's command center.

It is named after Samuel P. Capen, known as the Architect of UB. He became chancellor in 1922 and turned a loose group of independent schools into a modern university with 14 divisions and a central campus.
The name was borrowed. Capen Hall first belonged to a medical and dental building on South Campus. When the name moved north in 1977, the old building became Farber Hall.
It is about 310,000 square feet and was finished in June 1977 for about 6.2 million dollars.
Capen's own desk from around 1927 survives. It was in the presidential suite when President Tripathi took office in 2011.
orientation: The President, the Provost, Admissions and 1Capen all work in Capen Hall.
It also houses Silverman Library, the University Archives and The Poetry Collection.
The Honors College opened here in 2011.
Silverman Library got a 7.2 million dollar renovation from December 2014 to August 2016. During the work, its collections and study space moved to Lockwood.

alumni-arena.name: Alumni Arena
about: Broadview Arena was called Alumni Arena until it was renamed on March 11, 2026. If a senior says Alumni Arena, they mean this building.
The old name honored the nearly 100,000 people who had graduated from UB since 1846.
Broadview Federal Credit Union signed a 15-year, 31.75 million dollar partnership. It also renamed UB Stadium to Broadview Stadium, and named the area between them Broadview Village.
The deal funds student scholarships and the student emergency fund.
Famous visitors: the Harlem Globetrotters played here in 2012, and President Obama spoke to a sold-out crowd in 2013.
It was built in two phases from 1979 to 1985 for about 26.3 million dollars, designed by Buffalo architect Robert Traynham Coles.
orientation: The main gym seats 10,000 people. It hosts basketball, wrestling, volleyball, commencement and Distinguished Speaker Series talks.
There is also a triple gym, a wrestling room, a dance studio and a gymnastics area.
It has an eight-lane, Olympic-size pool.

davis.name: Davis Hall
about: Davis Hall opened on May 10, 2012.
It is named after Jack and Barbara Davis. Jack graduated from UB engineering in 1955. They gave 5 million dollars toward the building, and Jack said UB's education is what made him an engineer.
In 1964 Jack founded I Squared R Element Company, the only U.S. maker of certain heating elements used to produce display glass, fiber optics and solar panels.
Davis Hall is LEED Gold certified, and was named Best Educational Project in Business First's 2012 Brick By Brick awards.
orientation: Davis Hall is home base for Computer Science and Engineering, and Electrical Engineering.
It has smart rooms that adapt to how they are used.
It has clean rooms for nanotech, electronics and biomedical research.
It also houses the CEDAR and CUBS research centers.

student-union.name: Student Union
about: Students fought for this building. For years after 1982, UB had no real student union on either campus.

When Squire Hall, the South Campus union, closed on February 26, 1982, more than 200 students held a sit-in. Thirty-two refused to leave and were charged with criminal trespassing. President Ketter suspended them as his last act in office.
The Student Activities Center opened in 1984. In 1985, students passed a resolution calling it too small and demanding an expansion.
The expansion added about 110,000 square feet for 12.4 million dollars and finished almost a year early.
It was renamed the Student Union in April 1992 and dedicated that November, giving 75 clubs a home.
At the opening, President Greiner told students it was all theirs to shape.
UB celebrated a renovated grand reopening in January 2025.
orientation: The Student Union has been home to student clubs since it was dedicated in 1992.
It was renovated and reopened in January 2025.

cfa.name: Center for the Arts
about: The Center for the Arts, or CFA, is the skylit building at the end of Coventry Road.
It opened in 1994 as the Fine Arts Center and cost 50 million dollars.
The arts departments moved in during September 1993, before the stages were done. It was the first time all of UB's arts departments sat close together.
An opening festival ran from October 28 to November 20, 1994, and the Drama Theatre opened with The Threepenny Opera.
Ray Charles is among the artists who later performed here.
It was designed by Gwathmey Siegel of New York City.
orientation: CFA has four theatres. The largest is the 1,750-seat Mainstage. There is also the Drama Theatre, a Black Box Theatre and a screening room.
It has two art galleries, video and sound studios, dance studios, and even a metal foundry.
The atrium seats 600 and is a favorite meeting spot for students.

clemens.name: Clemens Hall
about: Clemens Hall is named for Samuel Clemens, better known as Mark Twain, who lived in Buffalo from 1869 to 1871.
In Buffalo, Twain lived at 472 Delaware Avenue and was editor and part-owner of the Buffalo Express. His first child, Langdon, was born here.
Twain gave the Huckleberry Finn manuscript to the public library's predecessor, but the first half went missing. It turned up in Los Angeles in 1991.
The full manuscript is now on display in the Mark Twain Room at the downtown Central Library.
In March 1989, a couch caught fire on the seventh floor, causing up to 25,000 dollars in smoke damage.
It was finished in May 1976 for about 5.4 million dollars, designed by Ulrich Franzen and Associates.
orientation: Clemens Hall has ten stories.
It holds Arts and Sciences administration, English, Romance Languages, Comparative Literature and American Studies.
The language labs are here too.
